$comment: GPD Forge — the API contract, and the arbiter for both sides of it. GPL-3.0-or-later.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. On 2026-08-28 the shipped app was unusable while every test was green.
AlertSeverity is a C# enum; without JsonStringEnumConverter the daemon emitted the ordinal 1
while the mock daemon, docs/api.md and types.ts all said "Aviso". The UI called
severity.toLowerCase() on a number, React unmounted the whole tree, and the window went black.
The E2E suite passed throughout because it only ever talked to the mock — and the mock had
always been right. A contract tested only against its own replica is not tested.
HOW IT WORKS. Neither side is compared to the other; both are compared to THIS FILE.
core.tests/ApiContractTests.cs   starts the real daemon and validates it here.
tests/e2e/contract.spec.ts       queries the mock daemon and validates it here.
A route the daemon gains but nobody declares fails the C# route-coverage test. Declaring it
then fails the mock test until the mock implements it. That chain is the point: it is what
makes it impossible to ship an endpoint the E2E suite has never seen.
TYPES. A field value is either a type string or an object.
"string" | "number" | "boolean" | "object" | "array"  — unions with '|', e.g. "number|null".
{ "type": "array", "items": { ...fields... } }  — items checked only when the array is
non-empty; an empty array is legitimately empty on a clean machine.
{ "type": "object", "fields": { ...fields... } }
{ "type": "string", "oneOf": [...] }  — the enum guard. This is the one that would have
caught the 2026-08-28 outage: an ordinal is not a string and 1 is not in the list.
MISSING vs EXTRA. Every declared field must be present — a field that silently stops being
emitted breaks a client. Undeclared extra fields are allowed, so this is a floor and adding to
a response is never a breaking change.
Shapes below were captured from the live daemon on 2026-08-31 (v0.2.0, commit a0a999f), not
written from the source. Re-capture rather than hand-edit when a response legitimately changes.
⚠️ AND CHECK NULLABILITY AGAINST THE TYPE, NOT THE CAPTURE. A capture shows what one machine
returned, not what the field is allowed to return. /display/tablet was declared non-null from a
reading of false/0 when the type is bool?/int? and null is the normal state of a machine that
has never set ConvertibilityEnabled. The mock guard caught it in its first run precisely because
the mock models the null case — which is the whole argument for validating both sides against
this file instead of against each other.

routes.$comment: `intentStapmW` added in F1 audit round 1 (2026-09-25): what the user wants in force (manual, else the game profile, else the mode's preset), where `stapmW` is the last write by ANY owner, a guardian throttle included. Every field nullable because 'nothing has written TDP since the daemon started' is a real answer and must not be dressed up as 0 W applied by nobody. `verified` is three-valued like the audit log, and `backend` is on the wire because with the hardware gate closed the stub echoes the request back and therefore 'verifies' every time — reporting verified without the backend would be a liar with a timestamp.

Quiet/Balanced/Aggressive added 2026-09-25 (F1). POST /fan has always accepted them (FanControlPolicy) and /panic sets Aggressive, so the old list failed the moment anyone picked one; a game profile now sets them automatically, which made the gap certain to bite.

One key per mode in core/Profiles/Modes.cs. ModeCatalogueTests already fails if a mode is missing from the C# preset table, the TypeScript union, the UI list or the mock — this entry adds the wire itself, so a mode cannot reach a release without a preset a client can read.
`overrides` added in F1 (2026-09-25): per-game stapmW, frameCapFps, fanMode, gpu { antiLag, chill } and freeze, each nullable. Null for a rule that only picks a mode — every seeded rule.

F1 (2026-09-25). The game profile in force, in memory: `active:false` with every field null after a restart and whenever auto-profiles are off, and for a rule that only picks a mode. `applied` is what the profile still holds, checked against each owner when asked; `skipped` what the rule asked for and was refused or is being held off, with why; `superseded` (audit round 1) names the fields the user changed since (stapmW, fanMode, frameCapFps), which leave `applied`; `freeze` is stored only until F5. core.tests/Profiles/ActiveGameProfileWireTests validates a POPULATED answer here.

latest.$comment: Declared down to the enums on purpose. When the converter was removed to falsify these guards, /alerts caught it and /alerts/summary did not — it carries the same alert object and was declared as a bare 'object'. One weak declaration is a hole the size of the whole endpoint.

routes.$comment: antiLag/chill added in F1 (2026-09-25): a game profile's Radeon features, layered over the mode's by the agent. Null = the mode decides. capVersion added in F1 audit round 4: rises on every cap request; with requestedAtUtc it is the request's identity, so the agent carries out a new request even when its value is the one it last wrote.

Added 2026-09-24. The service is in session 0, where the local foreground query is always null; `source: agent` means the user-session agent reported within the last 10 s. `process` is null on a clean machine with no agent, and `ageMs` is null whenever the source is local.

convertible and raw are bool?/int? in TabletModeService — null means ConvertibilityEnabled is not set and Windows is using default chassis detection. They were first declared non-null here because the capture came from a machine where the key happened to be set, and the mock guard caught it on its first run. See the note on capture in $comment at the top of this file.

canStopCharging is declared and is always false. A client that only saw the other fields could reasonably build a 'stop at 80%' switch; the field exists so the refusal is part of the contract rather than an omission. episodeHours is null with no episode running, never 0 — zero would read as an episode that just began.

Almost everything is nullable and that is the feature, not laxness. cycleCount and cellTemperatureC are null on this board because the EC does not report them, each with a stated reason field — the alternative is printing '0 cycles' next to '91% health' and leaving the user to resolve it.
Returns a bare array, not an object, so there are no root fields to declare. The route-existence and JSON-parseability checks still apply.

`fps01PctLow`, `stuttersPerMin`, `energyWh` (+ `energySource`: 'battery' drain or 'package' power), `mode` and `frameCapFps` added in F2 (2026-09-25). All null on sessions stored before F2 and whenever the reading behind them was never taken.

F3 Forge Advisor (2026-09-25). `?game=` asks about one game; without it, the game presenting frames (else the session recorder's current app), and game:null with empty lists when there is none. Each suggestion: { id ('kind:game[:value]'), game, kind (cap_refresh | cap_30 | lower_resolution | stapm_ceiling | fewer_watts), title, detail, stapmW|null, frameCapFps|null, applicable }. `applied`: { id, game, kind, stapmW, frameCapFps, atUtc }, newest first. Dismissed suggestions are left out.

F2 (2026-09-25): the target's frame times over the last 10 s, oldest first, capped to the newest 1000; metrics are computed over the whole 10 s before the cap. `available` false (and process/metrics null, frametimesMs empty) when the FPS gate is closed, PresentMon is absent, or nothing is presenting.
`packageAvgW` added in F1 (2026-09-25) for the Games page: duration-weighted like the FPS averages, null when no session read the package power.

Deliberately mock-only, and documented as such in docs/api.md — the mock implements SSE so the UI can be developed against a live-looking feed; production polls. Declared here so the mock guard tolerates it BY NAME rather than by allowing unknown extra routes in general, which would let a genuine phantom through.
Serves CSV, not JSON. Declared so route coverage sees it; body shape is not checked here.
Parameterised; needs a live id, so it is declared for coverage and exercised by sessions.spec.ts.
